data.name: About.Message
data.value:
diCAN — free and open-source CAN analyser software
V{0}. One adapter, one bus: receive aggregated by id or as a frame stream, periodic and one-shot transmit, recording to a database and export. Written as the official companion software for the DSD TECH SH-C3x adapters.

data.name: SessionType.Single.Description
data.value: One adapter, one bus. Normal, listen only, and loopback where the firmware supports it.

data.name: Mode.Silent
data.value: Listen only — never acknowledges, safe on someone else's bus

data.name: Mode.InternalLoopback
data.value: Internal loopback — hears itself, nothing reaches the wire

data.name: Mode.ExternalLoopback
data.value: External loopback — frames go out and come back

data.value: Delete “{0}” recorded at {2}, and its {1:N0} frames? This cannot be undone, and the space is not returned to the file.

data.value: Deleting a recording frees space inside the file but the file does not shrink. Compact rewrites each month so that space goes back to the disk. While it runs it needs room for a second copy of the file.

data.name: Recordings.Volume.Newer

data.name: Recordings.Empty.Filtered
data.value: No recording falls in this date range. Clear the dates to see them all.

data.name: Options.RecordFilteredOnly
data.value: Record only what the filter passes

data.name: Options.RecordFilteredOnlyNote
data.value: While this is ticked, every change to the filter is written into the recording, so a stretch of missing ids can be explained afterwards. Untick to record the whole bus.

data.name: Options.RecordRawTextNote
data.value: A second copy of every frame, exactly as the adapter sent it. Useful if the decoder is ever fixed and you want to read the capture again. It makes the file substantially larger, and much larger on CAN FD.

data.name: Options.AutoReconnect
data.value: Reconnect automatically after an unexpected disconnect

data.name: Options.AutoReconnectNote
data.value: Off by default: it puts the adapter back on the bus. Never runs when you press Disconnect; a recording continues.

data.name: Options.PollNote
data.value: Lower finds a newly plugged adapter sooner. One scan costs well under a millisecond.

data.name: Options.CapacityNote
data.value: When the buffer is full, each new frame replaces the oldest one. Increasing the capacity uses proportionally more memory.

data.name: Options.RestartNote
data.value: Refresh interval and stream size need a restart. Everything else is immediate.

data.name: Reconnect.GaveUp
data.value: Reconnecting failed after {0} attempt(s). Press Connect to try again.

data.name: Grid.LenNote
data.value: Payload length in bytes. For a remote frame this is the number of bytes requested, which is the only length such a frame has.

data.name: Grid.TypeNote
data.value: Blank for an ordinary classic data frame, which is most of them. FD is a CAN FD frame, FD BRS is CAN FD with the bit rate switched for the data phase, and RTR is a remote request carrying no payload. Standard and extended ids are told apart in the ID column instead: three hex digits when standard, eight when extended.

data.name: Detail.Empty
data.value: Select a row to see its full payload.

data.name: Display.DeltaNote
data.value: Both are the gap between two frames of one id. They come from host-side timestamps, which carry about ±100 µs of jitter. On a busy bus "min Δ" often reads 0.0 — that is the timestamp resolution, not the bus.

data.name: Display.DeltaTimeNote
data.value: Δ from the line above. Blank on the first line and after a gap, where there is nothing to measure against.

data.name: History.RemoveTip
data.value: Remove this one from the saved history

data.name: History.ClearAll.Message
data.value: This deletes all {0} saved filters, including those not shown in the list. It cannot be undone.

data.name: History.ClearAll.Failed
data.value: The history could not be deleted; the data is still on disk.

data.name: Record.NotWired
data.value: diCAN could not open the recording database on this computer, so frames are NOT being saved. The details have been written to the log.

data.name: Export.Csv.Hint
data.value: Carries everything: CAN FD, bit rate switching, remote frames, direction, and the raw slcan line when the recording kept one.

data.name: Export.Trc.Hint
data.value: Carries classic CAN, and CAN FD and remote frames as well, checked against PEAK's published format specification (not yet opened in PEAK software).

data.name: Export.Failed
data.value: Export failed. The details have been written to the log.

data.name: Export.Refused
data.value: Nothing was written: not one frame in this recording can be written to TRC. Export CSV instead.

data.name: Export.FilterNote
data.value: Only frames the current filter admits are recorded, so an export contains only those. If the filter is changed while recording, each change is stored with the recording.

data.name: Export.NotWired
data.value: The recording database could not be opened, so there is nothing to export. The details have been written to the log.

data.name: Tx.Hint
data.value:
Press Add for a new row. It arrives switched off, so nothing reaches the bus until you tick Enable — fill in the ID, data and period first. A blank repeat count means "until stopped"; 1 means send it once.
In the ID column, an ID of eight hex digits is a 29 bit (extended) frame, fewer digits is 11 bit, and an ID too big for 11 bits is refused — write it as eight digits to send it as a 29 bit frame.
Send now puts one frame out immediately, whether or not the row is switched on.

data.name: Transport.Rejected
data.value: The adapter rejected '{0}' without giving a reason.

data.name: Transport.NotOnBus
data.value: The adapter is not on the bus.

data.name: Transport.NoAnswer
data.value: The adapter did not answer '{0}' within {1:0.#} s. Every slcan firmware generation answers its commands or its version query, so this port is probably not an slcan adapter.

data.name: Transport.NoTimingLimits
data.value: This adapter did not report the CAN clock and bit timing limits, so the {0} sample point cannot be computed for it. Leave the sample point unset to use the adapter's own timing table.

data.name: Transport.NoExactTiming
data.value: This adapter's {0} MHz CAN clock cannot produce {1} bit/s exactly in the {2} phase, so no bit timing exists for it.

data.name: Transport.UnsupportedNominal
data.value: This adapter cannot do {0}. It supports {1}. ⛔ Nothing was sent.

data.name: Transport.UnsupportedData
data.value: This adapter cannot do a {0} data phase. It supports {1}. ⚠ The board's transceiver may be a lower ceiling still than this list. ⛔ Nothing was sent.

data.name: Transport.GsUsb.NoExactNominal
data.value: This device cannot produce {0} bit/s exactly from its {1} Hz CAN clock.

data.name: Transport.GsUsb.NoExactData
data.value: This device cannot produce a {0} bit/s data phase exactly.

data.name: Transport.GsUsb.NoEchoes
data.value: The adapter did not acknowledge any of the {0} frames already given to it within {1:0.#} s. The bus may be unterminated, bus-off, or have no other node to acknowledge frames.

data.name: Transport.GsUsb.NoLimitsAnswer
data.value: The device did not answer the bit timing limits request.

data.name: Transport.GsUsb.NoOneShot
data.value: This device cannot switch off automatic retransmission: it does not offer gs_usb one-shot mode. Leave automatic retransmission on, or use an adapter that does.

data.name: FilterError.Empty
data.value: A filter cannot be empty. Use <id>:<mask>, for example 7E0:7FF.

data.name: FilterError.NoColon
data.value: '{0}' has no ':'. A filter is <id>:<mask>, for example 7E0:7FF.

data.name: FilterError.TwoColons
data.value: '{0}' has more than one ':'. Separate several filters with ';'.

data.name: FilterError.IdTooLarge
data.value: id {0} does not fit in {1} bits (largest is {2}).

data.name: FilterError.MaskTooLarge
data.value: mask {0} does not fit in {1} bits (largest is {2}).

data.name: FilterError.PartMissing
data.value: The {0} is missing. A filter is <id>:<mask>, for example 7E0:7FF.

data.name: FilterError.PartTooLong
data.value: The {0} '{1}' has {2} hex digits; the most it can have is {3}.

data.name: FilterError.PartNotHex
data.value: The {0} '{1}' is not hexadecimal. Write it bare, without 0x: 7E0, not 0x7E0.

data.name: SendError.IdNotHex
data.value: '{0}' is not a hexadecimal CAN ID. Enter the ID using digits 0–9 and letters A–F.

data.name: SendError.IdTooLarge
data.value: {0} exceeds {1}, the largest 29-bit ID. Enter an ID within this limit.

data.name: SendError.IdTooLargeStandard
data.value: {0} is larger than {1}, the largest 11 bit id. Write the id as 8 hex digits to make it a 29 bit one.

data.name: SendError.FdHasNoRemote
data.value: CAN FD has no remote frames. The Type column offers one or the other, not both.

data.name: SendError.BrsNeedsFd
data.value: Bit rate switching only exists in CAN FD. Set the Type column to FD BRS, or choose a type without BRS.

data.name: SendError.OddHexDigits
data.value: Payload needs an even number of hex digits, two per byte.

data.name: SendError.DataNotHex
data.value: '{0}' is not hexadecimal. Use only digits 0–9 and letters A–F for each data byte.

data.name: SendError.DataTooLongFd
data.value: {0} bytes is more than the {1} a CAN FD frame carries. Shorten the data to fit within this limit.

data.name: SendError.DataTooLongClassic
data.value: {0} bytes is more than the {1} a classic CAN frame carries. Set the Type column to FD for longer payloads.

data.name: SendError.NoSuchFdLength
data.value: CAN FD does not support a data length of exactly {0} bytes. Choose one of these lengths: 0 to 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 48 or 64 bytes.

data.name: SendError.RemoteHasNoData
data.value: A remote frame carries no data. Clear the payload, or clear Remote.

data.name: SendError.RemoteLengthMissing
data.value: A remote frame needs the number of bytes it is requesting, 0 to {0}.

data.name: SendError.RemoteLengthNotNumber
data.value: '{0}' is not a whole number of bytes.

data.name: SendError.RemoteLengthTooLarge
data.value: A remote frame can request 0 to {0} bytes, not {1}.

data.value: This session joined the bus silently, so nothing here can transmit.

data.name: Send.ListenOnlyNote
data.value: This session opened in listen only, so sending is disabled. Reconnect and choose a different bus mode to transmit.

data.name: Send.SkippedNote
data.value: {0} transmission(s) skipped: this machine cannot keep up with the interval you asked for. The rate on the bus is lower than the one shown.

data.name: Status.Disconnected
data.value: {0} — disconnected. The table shows what was captured, and is no longer live.

data.name: Status.Paused
data.value: {0} — paused. The table has stopped refreshing; receiving and counting carry on, so nothing is being lost.

data.name: Status.PeriodNote
data.value: Period is a mean. Host side timestamps carry about 100 microseconds of jitter, so it is not a bus level measurement.

data.name: Filter.Hint
data.value: id:mask, several separated by ';'. 7E0:7FF is one id, 700:700 is a range, empty shows everything. In a filter, up to three hex digits means an 11 bit id and four or more means 29 bit.

data.name: FirmwareNotice.Intro
data.value: This adapter ships with CANable's factory firmware. DSD TECH publishes a more complete firmware for this adapter:

data.name: FirmwareNotice.Crystal
data.value: Clocked from the on-board 24 MHz crystal

data.name: FirmwareNotice.ModesHonoured
data.value: Listen-only and loopback actually take effect

data.name: FirmwareNotice.StaleFrames
data.value: Frames left unsent are not handed to the next session

data.name: FirmwareNotice.How
data.value: The firmware and the steps for changing it are on this board's product page:

data.name: Warn.NotConfirmed
data.value: This adapter does not acknowledge commands, so diCAN cannot confirm the bitrate took effect. What you see is what was requested, not what the device reports.

data.name: Guidance.Ready
data.value: Ready: diCAN can open this adapter.

data.name: Guidance.BootloaderUnplugTerminalBlock
data.value: Unplug the CAN terminal block, then unplug and reconnect USB while leaving the CAN terminal block disconnected. BOOT0 is also CAN_RX on this chip, so an idle bus can hold it high at power-up and boot the ROM instead of the firmware.

data.name: Guidance.BootloaderCheckBoot0Jumper
data.value: Put the board's own BOOT0 jumper or switch back. This chip has a dedicated BOOT0 pin, so the CAN bus cannot have caused it.

data.name: Guidance.BootloaderDisableBoot0Permanently
data.value: Once the firmware runs again, disable BOOT0 permanently with the slcan command *Boot0:Off.

data.name: Guidance.BootloaderRescan
data.value: Then rescan: the adapter should appear as an slcan or candlelight device.

data.name: Guidance.ReflashToSlcan25
data.value: Reflash it with the CANable 2.5 Slcan build and it will appear as a COM port (USB 16D0:117E).

data.name: Guidance.F072CannotRunSlcan25
data.value: This board cannot run CANable 2.5 at all, at any version. Its only slcan firmware is the original canable-fw.

data.name: Guidance.Legacy1ConfirmsNothing
data.value: This is the original CANable 1.0 firmware. It acknowledges no command, so diCAN cannot confirm that any setting it sends took effect.

data.name: Guidance.Legacy1NoCanFd
data.value: It has no CAN FD support at all.

data.name: Guidance.NoPortCheckDriverBinding
data.value: Recognised, but Windows has not assigned it a COM port. Check Device Manager for a warning icon on this device: that is a driver problem, not a device fault.

data.name: Guidance.NoSerialNodePublished
data.value: Recognised, but the system has not published a serial device for it, so there is nothing to open. Re-plug it, and try another port or cable.

data.name: Guidance.NothingFoundUsualCauses
data.value: diCAN does not recognise this USB device as a CAN adapter. The usual causes are a charge-only cable with no data lines, a hub that is not enumerating, or the device enumerating as something unexpected.
